shared_facts.value: The BA adapter must model source audit using structural snapshot fields from the SDK-backed adapter rather than access-log semantics [1, 2].
CLI-native entry points are the authoritative user-facing contract where they already exist in the repository [3].

The authoritative machine-readable audit shape includes source_id, title, source_type, status, is_ready, url, content, char_count, guide_summary, guide_keywords, and is_fresh; human presentation such as JSON vs. table output is a rendering choice rather than a separate contract requirement [2].
shared_facts.note: Repo-backed clarification: the structural snapshot data shape is authoritative, while terminal formatting remains presentation-specific.

shared_facts.value: Deterministic BA snapshotting must rely on SDK fulltext and snapshot data because MCP source content is capped and insufficient [2, 4, 5].

fe_facts.value: notebooklm source fulltext retrieves the uncapped source text [2, 6].
notebooklm source guide retrieves intelligence gathering metadata (summary and keywords) [2, 6].
notebooklm source stale checks for source freshness [2, 6].
notebooklm source refresh triggers a re-ingestion or update of the source [2, 6].
notebooklm source wait pauses execution until the source is ready [2, 6].

be_facts.value: src/notebooklm/_sources.py exposes get_fulltext(), get_guide(), check_freshness(), refresh(), and wait_until_ready() [6].

MCP source content is truncated to 50,000 characters or a configured maximum, making it unsuitable for canonical BA snapshots; high-fidelity audits must use SDK fulltext, guide, and freshness methods instead [2, 5].
be_facts.note: In the BA adapter, is_fresh is populated from client.sources.check_freshness() rather than derived from the capped MCP preview.

be_facts.value: Source intelligence commands (guide, refresh, freshness) are present in the SDK and CLI but entirely absent from the current MCP layer [6, 7].

notes: Sources provided highly specific field-level metadata for the audit shape and identified explicit CLI vs. MCP parity gaps.
The distinction between access-log semantics and structural snapshots was clearly resolved by decision [1].
The readiness blockers are resolved by treating the SDK-backed structural snapshot as authoritative and by explicitly excluding preview-capped MCP content from deterministic BA audit paths.
